correctness.rationale: The forcing closure proves a bijection between maximum failed sets and complements of minimum forts. For each blue cell the white neighbor count is exactly its row plus column occupancy. The exhaustive regimes (no empty lines, empty columns only, empty rows only, both empty) give lower bounds and all equality patterns; the thin-board overlapping case is counted once. Orbit counts follow from the intersection size of two 2-element column supports. An independent adjacency-based script tested 20 dimensions (360898 candidate subsets), plus eight direct forcing comparisons. Finite checks are corroborative; the proof is valid for every m,n>=2.

originality.rationale: The 2015 rook-graph theorem establishes only the extremal cardinality and exhibits a rectangle; the 2022 product treatment recalls that theorem without counting all maximizers. The 2024 fort-enumeration study treats different named families and generic join/corona/vertex-sum operations, and the general fort-hypergraph product papers do not imply the rook-specific smallest-fort multiplicities. The new comparison concerns a full parametric labeled enumeration, complete shape classification, and thin-board symmetry orbit counts. A previously available rook-fort extremal result gives the opposite extremum, the largest inclusion-minimal fort, not the minimum forts counted here. Index and literal searches remain inherently incomplete.
residual_risks: An unindexed or obscure treatment could enumerate minimum forts of line graphs of complete bipartite graphs using incidence-matrix terminology without the words rook graph or failed zero forcing.
Finite database tables or unpublished computational classifications might already include some small cases; no claim of independent publication-priority certification is made.

value.rationale: The natural zero-forcing extremizer-count question is unresolved by the known scalar formula. The theorem identifies every optimizer, computes exact labeled multiplicities for all rook graphs, and detects nontrivial thin-board orbit types and three exceptional rectangle families. It thereby specifies the minimum-cardinality stratum of a natural fort hypergraph, useful for extremal structure and fort-cover models. This is not a textbook substitution or merely numerical recomputation.
